messages:
maria g: Heads-up — saw a big queue depth spike (~4x) in the us-west GPU pool during the nightly spot migration window at ~03:14 UTC. Batch size dropped to 1 on a lot of workers and latency jumped. Grafana spike attached :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jon p: ugh, that sounds like the spot preemptions again. Do we have correlation with node drain events or k8s evictions?

akshay k: I pulled logs — kubelet evict and pod deletion events line up with the time window. GCE preemptible drain notices show a flurry between 03:10–03:17.

maria g: Confirmed. The autoscaler didn't provision fast enough because our scale-up signal comes from available_nodes, but the queue-based policy waits for queue depth > threshold for 60s. By the time it tripped, pods were already in Terminating and batch sharding caused many small batches.

lisa r: Do we have a Grafana panel that shows "steady-state batch_size" vs "active_workers"? I want to see the shape.

maria g: Yep — panel name "pool_batch_shape" in infra dashboard. Two notes: the histogram is 30s buckets so the spike looks sharper than raw samples. Also, the alert we're using for "queue-depth-high" fires on an instant vector > 200 which produced noisy triggers during preemption storms.

jon p: Proposal: treat spot migration windows as a different SLO curve. Two quick fixes: 1) change alert to require 2+ consecutive 30s intervals (i.e., 90s sustained) and use a quantile (p95) of queue depth rather than instant; 2) add a short-circuit to scale by node_creation_rate when preemption events > X/min.

akshay k: I can prototype a PromQL rule for p95 queue depth: ```
# p95 queue depth over 1m using histogram_quantile over rate of observations
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(queue_depth_bucket[1m])) by (le, pool))
```
Then an alert like: ```
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(queue_depth_bucket[1m])) by (le, pool)) > 150
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "p95 queue depth high in {{ $labels.pool }}"
```
This reduces flapping from short preemption blips.

maria g: Nice. Also want to add a separate emergency throttle: if node_preempt_events_total rate > 5/min AND queue_depth p95 > 100 => increase target nodes by +20% immediately. That prevents tiny batches from exploding cost/latency while autoscaler catches up.

lisa r: We should also add a Grafana heatmap of batch_size distribution over time (heatmap rather than timeseries) so SREs can eyeball when batches collapse to 1.

jon p: Agree. Ops runbook update: when "preempt storm" occurs -> 1) mute low-priority alerts, 2) set a temporary scale override for pool us-west-gpu for 10m, 3) collect kubelet logs from affected nodes (use node label filter), 4) escalate to cloud infra if preempt rate persists >10/m for 5m.

akshay k: I'll open a PR with Prometheus rule + Grafana panel JSON. Will add tests for the alert rule using the alertmanager test harness (simulate preempt spike + queue growth).

maria g: Thanks. Action items: @akshay k PR for rules+panel, @jon p update runbook + create an incident template for preempt storms, @lisa r add heatmap to infra dashboard, and I'll run a canary of the quick scale override next maintenance window.

ops-bot: Incident template created: "preempt-storm-template" (incident-3571). Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/preempt-storm

lisa r: One more ask — can we add a small gauge metric: "batch_shrink_events_total" when a worker's average batch_size falls below 2 for >30s? That would give a direct signal for this class of failure.

akshay k: good idea. I can add an exporter counter on the serving runtime to emit that. Will include in PR.

maria g: Great. If everyone is OK, let's land the alert change as non-blocking (recording rule + alert tweak) and the Grafana heatmap in the next 48 hours. Then follow up with the runtime export + autoscale short-circuit in the next sprint. :thumbsup:

jon p: 👍

akshay k: on it.

lisa r: thanks all.
